title: The suspected malware click — question explanation
learningObjective: Select appropriate reporting, containment and evidence-preservation steps
format: 16:9 educational motion-graphics video; narration; separate captions; no autoplay with sound
visualStyle: Deep navy and charcoal; restrained cyan/electric-blue highlights; limited purple accents; clean typography; purposeful, low-motion transitions; accessible contrast.

scenes.name: Scenario setup
scenes.visual: You opened a suspicious attachment on a managed laptop. The device is behaving unusually, and your organization has an incident-response number.
scenes.direction: Show a fictional simulated setting. Use generic UI and no actual organization, brand, user identity, credential, real URL or live account.

scenes.name: Learning objective and risk cue
scenes.visual: Select appropriate reporting, containment and evidence-preservation steps
scenes.direction: Highlight only observable cues and explain the decision context without implying certainty beyond the scenario.

scenes.name: Recommended response
scenes.visual: Option B: Immediately follow the organization’s incident procedure, report the event, and isolate the device if policy or responders direct you to. Prompt reporting and coordinated containment are safer than improvising remediation.
scenes.direction: Animate the recommended defensive choice as a clear decision path. Display the action verb and trusted channel/control.

scenes.name: Why the other options fail
scenes.visual: Option A: Public upload may disclose confidential information and spread malware. Option C: Deleting files or logs can destroy evidence needed for investigation. Option D: Continuing activity or using unapproved tools can worsen impact or interfere with response.
scenes.direction: Show each unsafe alternative separately with a complete, concise reason. Do not depict operational exploitation, malicious code or credential capture.

scenes.name: Defensive takeaway
scenes.visual: Contact the organization’s security team immediately. Follow their containment instructions and preserve the device and relevant details. Report quickly and follow the incident-response plan; do not improvise forensic actions.
scenes.direction: Close with one readable takeaway and the next safe action. Keep the final frame long enough for comprehension.
scenes.onScreenText: Report quickly and follow the incident-response plan; do not improvise forensic actions.

narration: Scenario: You opened a suspicious attachment on a managed laptop. The device is behaving unusually, and your organization has an incident-response number. Safest response: Option B: Immediately follow the organization’s incident procedure, report the event, and isolate the device if policy or responders direct you to. Prompt reporting and coordinated containment are safer than improvising remediation. Option A is unsafe because Public upload may disclose confidential information and spread malware. Option C is unsafe because Deleting files or logs can destroy evidence needed for investigation. Option D is unsafe because Continuing activity or using unapproved tools can worsen impact or interfere with response. In practice: Contact the organization’s security team immediately. Follow their containment instructions and preserve the device and relevant details. Key takeaway: Report quickly and follow the incident-response plan; do not improvise forensic actions.
